brief: windF is a coin, not a scalar, and it is the most widely-read scalar in the town. #154 histogrammed it AT THE CALL: 0 on 257 samples and exactly 1.0 on 134 of 446, because `windTarget()` (~line 1503) is `Math.max(windyDay() ? 1 : 0, frontWind())`. So every term keyed on a windF strictly between 0 and 1 — awning and washing-line sway, the water mirror's chop (#145), the streaks, and #154's own PUNT_WIND_SLOW/PUNT_WIND_SHY — is a ramp nobody stands in. Give the day a real wind STRENGTH with a distribution: a breezy day should not be a gale, and a still day should not be dead flat. Then go back through the consumers — anything tuned against a 0/1 input is now mis-tuned, and the interesting ones are those whose response has never been visible.
successLooksLike: A histogram of windF at the call over a year x 3 seeds has real mass in the middle — no more than ~60% of samples at the two ends, against 88% (391 of 446) on HEAD — and a cropped difference image shows at least two consumers visibly differing between a windF 0.4 day and a windF 0.9 day.
avoid: `isWindy` (the behaviour boolean) and `windF` (the 0..1 intensity that draw sites multiply) are deliberately split — keep them split. This adds draws, so the seeded world reshuffles: read the census for COLLAPSE rather than delta, and replay every stray motion gate on HEAD before believing it.
